question.problem:
Let $V=C[0,2]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,2],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

If $x(t)=t$ and $y(t)=k-5{t}^{3}$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}t(k-5{t}^{3})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(kt-5{t}^{4})\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{k{t}^{2}}{2}-{t}^{5}){|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2k-32.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x(t),y(t)⟩ & =0 \\ 2k-32 & =0 \\ 2k & =32 \\ k & =16\end{aligned}
$$
